---
title: "Accounts"
---

The live agent examples use a Google account and a Gemini API key. A GitHub account supports collaboration and optional educational benefits. Account preparation is separate from installing Python: the offline exercises remain available while access to an external service is pending.

## Google account and AI Studio

An existing Google account can be used, or a new account can be created through [Google's account page](https://www.google.com/intl/en/account/about/). Signing in to [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/) establishes whether the account can access the service. Institutional accounts may have administrative restrictions.

The [AI Studio API Keys page](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey) manages Gemini credentials. After any required terms have been reviewed and accepted, an available project can be selected and a key created. AI Studio may already have created a default project and key for a new account. Existing Cloud projects may need importing before they appear. Google's [API-key documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-key) describes the current workflow and permission requirements.

The course uses the Gemini Developer API. Separate Vertex AI configuration is unnecessary for this route. API availability, quotas, and possible charges depend on the account and selected model; a Google account alone does not establish usable API access.

## Store the key locally

The key belongs in the course root's local `.env` file as `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. The [project setup chapter](03-project-setup.qmd) explains copying `.env.example`, setting `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI=FALSE`, and checking that Git ignores `.env`. Shared files and screenshots must contain placeholders rather than credentials.

## GitHub and student benefits

A [GitHub account](https://github.com/join) supports repository work. An existing account can retain its current identity: the university email address can be added in account settings and verified through the confirmation email.

The [GitHub Student Developer Pack](https://education.github.com/pack) is optional. GitHub checks student eligibility and may require evidence of current enrolment in addition to a verified academic email. Approval and the included benefits follow GitHub's current rules; the course does not depend on approval. The [official application guide](https://docs.github.com/en/education/about-github-education/github-education-for-students/apply-to-github-education-as-a-student) lists the requirements.

## Exercise: record account readiness

A short preparation record distinguishes Google sign-in, AI Studio access, API-key availability, and GitHub sign-in. It records only status, never the key itself. If AI Studio denies access, the record includes the error category and whether the account is institutionally managed.

**Expected result:** the credentials route is clear before the first live example. Offline work can proceed when API access remains pending. Student Pack approval is optional and is recorded separately.
